content.title: About
content.content: Canned plum consists of whole plum fruits that have been blanched, pitted and packed in glass or metal jars with syrup or their own juice. The fruit is harvested at the end of summer and quickly canned to preserve its sweet‑tart flavor, aroma and most of its nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plum belongs to the Rosaceae family and is closely related to peaches, apricots and cherries.
Canning allows plums to be stored for several years without loss of taste.
Plum pits contain amygdalin, which can release small amounts of cyanide in the body; therefore pits are removed during canning.
Traditionally plums are canned in a sugar syrup, but today many brands offer versions in their own juice with no added sugar.
Plum orchards have a long history in Europe, Asia and North America.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Plums provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and phenolic compounds in plums help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Plum fiber aids normal digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned plums contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Many canned plums are packed in sweet syrup, which raises their glycemic index and may be unsuitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to plums.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The natural acidity of plums can irritate the stomach in people with high gastric acidity.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some brands use food preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive to them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned plums can be eaten straight from the jar, added to desserts, yogurts, oatmeal, salads, or used in baking. They pair well with cinnamon, ginger and vanilla. The juice can be drained and used in sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep the jar refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors or color changes.
